parsed.explanation: The combined regime shows no visitor-facing restriction: decriminalisation since 1993, no gender-expression offence, no facility or document regime reaching travellers, and entry screening is not documented as trans-adverse. Hate-crime provisions cover gender identity, and police guidelines require detention by identified gender — but enforcement is documented weak, with complaints often unpunished. Documented violence (2001, 2009, 2014) is dated and individual, not a current trans-specific campaign; the worst documented feature is societal hostility with thin recourse (tier 3), plus an open question about outlying provinces. Dated LGBT-wide surveys are not trans-specific prevalence. The score sits in Reduced Risk, low end: no state targeting, no criminalisation, protections on paper, but social hostility with weak recourse.

entry_documents.protection: No trans-specific border friction documented; 2009 civil-registration change is resident-facing only.
entry_documents.interaction: Visitor documents are home-issued; no documented mismatching exposure at entry.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: A 2019 case of an officer assaulting a detained transgender woman.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Police guidelines (2019) require addressing transgender detainees by identified gender regardless of documents; current status beyond 2019 unsourced.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Training programme reached hundreds of police, prosecutors, judges.

care_services.exposure: Not documented; transition access described in capital profile but not visitor-specific.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Hyper-nationalist and neo-Nazi violence (2001, 2009, 2014); fear of police victimisation deters reporting; attacks often unpunished.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate-crime aggravation for gender identity since 2017; police/judiciary training; bias motive recording post-2014 reform unclear.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Enforcement of protections documented weak despite training.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented for visitors; 2019 survey shows LGBT youth bullying nationally (dated, LGBT-wide).
minors_guardians.protection: Sex-education curriculum includes SO/GI topics, teacher-optional.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented kidnapping, sexual assault and beating of trans women (2009); most recent attack 2014; strongly heteronormative society, harassment persists systemically; no venues or visible scene outside capital.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate-crime statute and 500+ trained officials; hate speech on gender identity outlawed.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response documented unreliable; complaints often disregarded.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Weak hate-crime enforcement; no comprehensive equality law; conditions outside capital undocumented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Constitutional and penal discrimination bars since 2015/2017; groups can register.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse exists in law but is documented as rarely effective for victims.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor shows a visitor stopped, detained, then receiving working remedies (apology, compensation). Here remedies are documented weak — attacks often unpunished — so this dossier sits below 0.65-A, though no visitor stop is documented at all.

0.55-E documents selective transit-police harassment and stalled investigations against visitors. Here no visitor-facing harassment is documented; the hostility is societal and dated incidents; weak enforcement parallels the stalled-remedy element, so this case sits modestly above.

0.35-A has universal, state-run exclusion machinery reaching every visitor. Nothing comparable exists here — no register, no facility ban, no checkpoint identity regime — so this jurisdiction is clearly above the High Risk boundary.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime combines decriminalisation, gender-identity-inclusive hate-crime law, and no documented traveller-facing restriction, against a strongly heteronormative society with documented nationalist violence (dated 2001–2014, none since) and police who disregard complaints. The worst documented feature is tier 3: societal hostility with thin recourse, not state targeting or universal exposure. Protections are real on paper but enforcement is weak; training and detainee guidelines are partial positives whose currency beyond 2019 is unsourced. Dated LGBT-wide surveys carry little weight. Weak signals are extrapolated from structural facts: no criminalisation, functioning registration of groups, trained institutions, but documented impunity. This places the jurisdiction at the lower edge of Reduced Risk: a visitor faces no institutional barrier, but if outed, remedy against social or police hostility is uncertain and often absent, and the outlying-provinces picture is unknown.
